source: Donella Meadows, Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System (1999). Rank 12 = weakest, 1 = strongest.

leverage_points.name: Constants, parameters, numbers (subsidies, taxes, standards)
leverage_points.question: Are we tuning dials on a machine whose design is the problem?
leverage_points.note: Parameters matter least — even the biggest dial rarely changes system behavior. People argue here because it is easiest, not because it works.

leverage_points.name: Sizes of buffers relative to flows
leverage_points.question: Would a bigger/smaller stabilizing stock change the system's resilience?
leverage_points.note: Buffers (inventory, runway, slack, cache) absorb shocks. Too big = lethargy; too small = brittleness. Often the cheapest structural fix.

leverage_points.name: Structure of material stocks and flows (network topology)
leverage_points.question: Where things physically accumulate and route — does the plumbing itself create the behavior?
leverage_points.note: Rewiring who-receives-what-from-whom changes behavior permanently. Slow, physical, expensive, durable.

leverage_points.name: Lengths of delays relative to rates of change
leverage_points.question: Is the system reacting to last month's signal at this month's speed?
leverage_points.note: Oscillation and overshoot are almost always delay mismatches. Shorten feedback delay or slow the action rate — one of the two, always.

leverage_points.name: Strength of negative (balancing) feedback loops
leverage_points.question: Does reality actually correct error here, and fast enough?
leverage_points.note: Balancing loops keep the system on goal. Strengthening the error signal (honest, timely measurement) beats adding new controls.

leverage_points.name: Gain around driving (reinforcing) loops
leverage_points.question: What is the compounding rate, and who benefits from it staying high?
leverage_points.note: Growth engines are also collapse engines. The gain that builds the empire runs the ruin — govern it before it governs you.

leverage_points.name: Structure of information flows (who sees what, when)
leverage_points.question: Does the actor causing the consequence ever experience it as information?
leverage_points.note: Adding a feedback loop of INFORMATION (not punishment) is often the highest value-for-effort intervention that exists.

leverage_points.name: Rules of the system (incentives, punishments, constraints)
leverage_points.question: Who wrote the rules, whom do they favor, and what behavior do they make rational?
leverage_points.note: Changing rules changes every player's rational strategy at once. Powerful, contested, and usually traceable to someone's interest.

leverage_points.name: Power to add, change, or self-organize system structure
leverage_points.question: Can the parts reconfigure themselves when reality shifts, or does every change need the center?
leverage_points.note: Self-organizing systems adapt faster than any planner. Rule-of-thumb: subordinate to the goal it optimizes toward.

leverage_points.name: Goals of the system
leverage_points.question: What is the single variable the whole machine is actually optimizing?
leverage_points.note: Change the goal and every loop, rule, and actor re-orients around it. Second-highest leverage; requires authority that matches.

leverage_points.name: Mindset or paradigm out of which the system arises
leverage_points.question: What must everyone believe for this system to make sense? Invert that belief — what becomes possible?
leverage_points.note: Paradigms are the source of systems. Keep rising them in the abstract and they self-propagate; one information-package at a time.

leverage_points.name: Power to transcend paradigms
leverage_points.question: Which paradigm are we currently blind inside of?
leverage_points.note: Holding all paradigms loosely — staying unattached to any single way of seeing — is the ultimate leverage point, and it cannot be held onto.
